subtype: Approach: choosing a fixed slot in the weekly timetable [Action]
passage: Manav had wanted to learn chess ever since the big tournament on television, but hobbies always melted into the evening. So he took a pencil to the family timetable pinned in the kitchen. Homework finishes by five. Tuesday and Saturday, five-thirty to six-thirty: chess. He wrote it in blue ink. At dinner he read it out to his mother Minakshi and his sister Indu. "Those are my chess hours. Please do not plan anything else then." Indu snorted; Minakshi smiled and moved the shopping trip to Wednesday. On Tuesday Manav set up the board at five-thirty exactly, and the house went quiet around him.

qa.q: On which days did Manav plan his chess hour?
qa.a: Manav planned his chess hour on Tuesday and Saturday.

qa.q: What was Manav feeling as he read the timetable aloud at dinner?
qa.a: Hopeful and a little nervous about whether the family would respect his time.

qa.q: What could Manav do if something clashes with a chess slot?
qa.a: Swap the slot to another day and tell the family, because a moved slot keeps the routine going.

qa.q: How might Minakshi see Manav's timetable?
qa.a: As a sign of real commitment, since she smiled and moved the shopping trip to Wednesday. 🙂

grounding: A boy fits chess into fixed slots after homework on two evenings and tells his family so the time is respected.

subtype: Approach: choosing a fixed slot in the weekly timetable [Action]
passage:
"Mummy, Papa, Parveen Didi, I've made a plan," Chetan announced, holding up a sheet. "Chess. Tuesday and Saturday, seven to eight."
"After homework?" Papa asked.
"After homework. Tuesday I only have maths and Hindi, so I'm done by seven. Saturday there's no homework."
Parveen raised an eyebrow. "Saturday seven is when we watch the quiz show."
"That's why I'm telling you now. Can you keep the TV low for that hour? I'll set up the board in my room."
"And who will you play?" Mummy asked.
"The puzzle book Nanaji gave me. Just for that hour."
Papa stuck the sheet on the fridge. "Then Tuesday and Saturday at seven, nobody sends Chetan on errands."
"Not even for bread?" Parveen asked, smirking.

qa.q: Which days and times did Chetan choose for chess?
qa.a: He chose Tuesday and Saturday, seven to eight.

qa.q: Why did Chetan tell his family about the plan at dinner?
qa.a: He felt hopeful about the plan but a bit worried that TV and errands would eat into the hour, so he wanted everyone to protect it.

qa.q: What else could help Chetan stick to his two slots?
qa.a: He could tick off each session on the fridge sheet, so after a few weeks he can see whether the slots really work and adjust them.

qa.q: How might the plan look to Parveen?
qa.a: She teases him, and she has to keep the quiz show quieter on Saturdays, so she may feel mildly put out while still going along with it 😅.

grounding: Shows a boy fixing two weekly chess hours after homework and telling his family so the time is respected.

subtype: Approach: choosing a fixed slot in the weekly timetable [Action]
passage: I'm Tarun, and last month my chess plan was "whenever I'm free". I was never free. Homework, then cartoons with my little sister Aditi, then dinner, then sleep. The chess set my uncle gave me sat in its box. So I looked at the week and picked two slots: Tuesday after homework, because Tuesdays are light, and Saturday at six, before dinner. One hour each. At dinner I told everyone. Mum wrote it on the kitchen calendar. Now on Tuesdays Aditi knocks on my door and says, "Bhaiya, it's chess time, I'm not allowed to disturb you," which is a disturbance, but a nice one. I've finished eleven puzzles from the book so far.

qa.q: Where did Mum write the chess slots?
qa.a: Mum wrote them on the kitchen calendar.

qa.q: How did Tarun seem to feel while the chess set sat in its box?
qa.a: Tarun seems to have felt frustrated and a bit guilty that "whenever I'm free" never actually came.

qa.q: Why might fixed slots work better for Tarun than "whenever I'm free"?
qa.a: Fixed slots give chess a real place in the week and let Tarun's family protect it, while a vague plan keeps losing to cartoons and dinner.

qa.q: What is chess time like for Aditi?
qa.a: Aditi seems to enjoy being part of it, proudly reminding Tarun that she isn't allowed to disturb him, even though the reminder is a small interruption itself.

grounding: A boy recalls moving chess from a vague plan to two fixed weekly slots and telling his family.
